findings.title: Controlled canceled changes still trigger validation
findings.suggested_fix: Carry cancellation for the initiating controlled change into the value-change synchronization path, and skip validation/error clearing for that canceled change while retaining synchronization for accepted programmatic prop changes.
evidence: packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx:139-145: onChange creates details, calls onValueChange, then immediately returns for controlled input without checking details.isCanceled.
packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx:153: uncontrolled path gates validation on both !event.nativeEvent.defaultPrevented and !details.isCanceled.

testing_gaps: The cancellation test exercises only an uncontrolled Field.Control. Add a controlled case whose onValueChange updates the prop and then cancels, and assert that validation is not called.

Rejected and rewritten controlled values are not tested for leaving field state and validation untouched. The controlled user-change test uses an accepting setter (FieldControl.test.tsx:97-114), while the programmatic-change test covers only an accepted update (142-167).
The cancellation test asserts only that validation is skipped (FieldControl.test.tsx:189-200); it does not check whether cancellation also prevents dirty/filled changes or clearing existing errors.

Programmatic synchronization tests only an empty-to-nonempty transition (FieldControl.test.tsx:142-167). A programmatic reset to the initial empty value is not checked for clearing filled and dirty state.

The new tests cover a programmatic controlled update and single validation, but not an out-of-order async validation race initiated by controlled prop updates. The existing FieldRoot async supersession test exercises the shared validation commit generation mechanism through an uncontrolled input.

residual_risks: A later non-undefined controlled value supersedes an older async commit through useFieldValidation’s generation check. A controlled-to-uncontrolled transition skips validation.change, so it does not itself invalidate a pending commit; React generally discourages changing control mode.
Pending async commits are not invalidated on Field.Control unmount. This is pre-existing validation lifecycle behavior, though the new path can start such work from a programmatic value change.
testing_gaps: No test verifies that an async validator for controlled value A cannot publish after a programmatic change to B.
No test verifies the result of controlled-value async validation resolving after Field.Control unmounts while Field.Root remains mounted.
